name: Драугр
quality_note: The built-in tool exposes no steps, quality or compute budget setting. Deliberate multi-reference prompts and review are used.

variants.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / professional game vehicle concept development.
Design ONE substantially re-engineered pirate RH light fighter named DRAUGR, evolved from the Banshee in Freelancer (2003). Deliver a highly considered art-director quality THREE-VIEW design sheet. The user rejected two prior attempts because they simply retained the stock silhouette and added panels. This attempt MUST invent new LARGE SHAPES and functional mechanical assemblies, changing the outer hull silhouette substantially while preserving the original cabin module and real mechanisms. A menacing pirate war machine assembled deliberately from donor industrial ship parts, capable and coherent, not a pile of garbage. Its demonic character must survive an untextured solid-color silhouette test.

REFERENCE ROLES:
Image 1 = actual stock rh_pir_fighter in flight; use for baseline scale, low cabin, elevated rear fixed core, wing locations and SINGLE engine, but actively REDESIGN the outer hull around those anchors. Do not trace the stock circular outer outline and rectangular neck.
Image 2 = original CABIN, the one IMMUTABLE external module; carefully reproduce the entire cabin, original proportions, framing, glass and chin.
Image 3 = actual cargo mechanism, closed and open: a RECTANGULAR dorsal hatch just behind the cockpit slides AFT and slightly UP, slipping back under the raised rear shoulder. This is NOT a rotating hatch and NOT a lower jaw. Design around this.
Image 4 = native TWO-PART wings shown flight, middle, folded. Final art uses FLIGHT only, like left column: swept FORWARD in top view, slightly drooping DOWN/OUT in front. Preserve sliding root and separate outer hinge.

KEEP THESE ANCHORS, REINVENT EVERYTHING BETWEEN:
Compact and deep fighter, approximately original W10.9 H7.1 L13.6, not an elongated transport, wide bomber or sleek jet. Original cabin hangs low at the very front. Elevated narrow rear core is a vertical circular disk with broad round faces looking SIDEWAYS port/starboard, not a forward-facing fan. Retain a recognizable round inset mechanical core but freely replace the OUTER outline with distinct angular closed armour masses. Do NOT insist on a fully circular stock perimeter. The rear core is stationary. Exactly ONE axial rear engine and ONE central exhaust, no extra thruster pods.
New neck and aft outer armour should have changed depth, incisive diagonal cuts, layered large continuous volumes and dramatic angular overhangs, not merely surface plates on a stock box. Primary silhouette first, substantial medium-scale mechanical detail second, paint last.
Preserve the original CABIN exactly: tall blunt faceted down-hanging nose, large sloping blue front windshield, narrow black/yellow horizontal divider with a lower blue glazing band, tall trapezoid/triangular side panes, broad original metal frames, small overhanging brow, original opaque stepped chin, red side inset, small lower blue corner slots, black/yellow bumper band and tapered underside point. Do not shrink it, reshape glass, add new cockpit armour, horns, a skull face, teeth, eye-like lights or a modern bubble canopy. The NEW hull attaches BEHIND this untouched module.

FUNCTIONAL DESIGN, VISIBLE MECHANISMS:
A substantial CLOSED wing-root sliding cartridge on EACH side below the neck, with a broad recessed guide channel and nested solid overlapping sleeves. At the elbow, a clearly identifiable cylindrical hinge bearing partially enclosed in an angular housing, joining the distinct inner and outer wing segments. These functional assemblies should be visibly more developed than the source, not tiny lines. Two wings total; no extra wings/fins used to fake the mechanism.
Flight wings sweep forward, downward droop, and use pointed hard angular broad surfaces of meaningful thickness. Outer sections roll UP ~63 degrees during docking; inner sections slide IN/UP/AFT. Keep clear gaps at moving boundaries and room to sweep. No fixed plate or strut bridges a hinge. All final views are the same unfolded FLIGHT condition.
Cargo door: leave a distinct flat rectangular inset sliding lid on the dorsal centerline of the neck BEHIND the cabin, clearly visible in TOP and 3/4. It translates AFT by about a quarter of ship length and rises only slightly. Keep a continuous central travel corridor and rear pocket. New dorsal spikes/shoulders are to the SIDES of that corridor, never a solid central obstruction. Show the cargo lid CLOSED in all three views; a single small fine arrow on TOP may label "BAYDOOR / SLIDES AFT". No detached inset, no new folding bottom door. The rear circular core never rotates with the cargo lid.
Mechanics should read as hard industrial engineering: a segmented solid engine shroud, two or three deep closed-backed ventilation pockets with broad blades, recessed service panels of different depths, shaped angular bearing covers, clear mounting sockets, substantial drive housings. Several intentional details per principal mass with quiet planes between; richness through large and medium geometry, not thousands of greebles.
NO exposed pipes, rods, hoses or cables. NO skeletal external frames, open trusses, cross-braces, roll cages or ladder-like structures. NO decorative rivet forests, tiny bolts, jewelry, uniformly spaced ribs or disconnected surface boxes. No giant guns used as a substitute for design; keep plausible hardpoint mounting pads clear. No skulls, flags, Rheinland military crosses, occult symbols or excessive rust. Sharp authored points and corners; do not round every edge.

ART:
Classic Freelancer Rheinland industrial geometry reworked by organized pirates. Worn charcoal steel, oxidized warm gray, a few purposeful pale donor armour sections and dark oxblood red fields. Original cabin retains its familiar pale shell and blue glazing. Strong controlled value separation to show all mechanical forms; not black-on-black. Pirate character comes from rebuilt structural shapes, layered donor housings and aggressive proportions, not paint alone. Restrained wear, no noisy grime obscuring forms. Convincing premium marker/gouache concept illustration with precise ink contours, dimensional shading and readable mechanics. Not photorealistic, no game background.
ONE landscape sheet, exactly THREE consistent views of the SAME concept: a large front-side 3/4 filling LEFT half, a true orthographic SIDE upper RIGHT with nose RIGHT, and a true orthographic TOP lower RIGHT with nose UP. ALL full silhouettes uncropped, adequate space, no overlapping views. SIDE and TOP must rigorously describe the same geometry, not just reuse stock outlines. Light warm ivory paper. Title as specified, small labels SIDE / FLIGHT and TOP / FLIGHT. No prose paragraphs or decorative border.

D01 SPECIFIC FORM: A powerful demonic-looking tall rear cowl, like a split angular crown built from INDUSTRIAL ENGINE CASINGS. Preserve the inner circular core, but bury its upper/rear portions inside a massive faceted dark armour cowl with a clearly changed polygonal outer profile. The cowl divides into TWO sharp solid dorsal shoulder crests, one on each side of the centerline; each rises from a continuous wedge surface and ends in a forward-leaning chisel point. They are not added animal horns or thin fins. Their broad thick bases taper naturally out of the armoured shoulders, with a central slot maintaining cargo-lid clearance. In side view give the top a purposeful two-level hooked wedge outline instead of the stock round dome. Show the circular side core deeply recessed behind two or three chunky unequal fixed armour sectors; use a dark red stepped semicircular mechanical seat with broad notches, not a flat shield with a cross. The solid lower cowl flows forward into a sculpted two-level angular neck sidewall, with one deep oblique vent and a sharply recessed lower channel. The original cabin remains at the end of this entirely new neck.
Wings: short and formidable forward-swept CHISEL wings, thick elbow hinge housings, a strong forward-pointing apex on each outer section and a single angular notch in its trailing edge; retain baseline span, articulate drooping flight posture, no stock rectangular tip. Each sliding wing root is an obvious heavy closed cartridge seated deeply within the underside of the neck. Engine ends in a short polygonal collar with two recessed broad vent fields. Pale donor plates limited to a few large facing surfaces, oxblood inner recesses, mostly charcoal and warm metal. The split high rear cowl and chiselled wing tips should make the new silhouette immediately distinguishable from Banshee.
Title exactly: DRAUGR / D01

One broad top armour slope descends toward the nose on each SIDE of the cargo-lid corridor; each side shoulder projects forward to a hard chisel end BEHIND the original cabin, stopping outside its glass. Sculpt these as coherent closed claw-like hull volumes, not decorative bones, framing bars or added thin spikes. Let the lower sidewall rise inward into a deep angular waist above the wing mechanism, creating a strong undercut in SIDE view and a narrow center between broader aft shoulders and the unchanged forward cabin. Two broad deep triangular/rectangular recessed vents interrupt the flank. The rear core is visibly recessed within an unequal lower angular crescent and upper wedge housing, with two or three large service segments. In TOP, the shoulders form a deliberate sharp fork around the unobstructed central sliding baydoor. Keep the central rear core narrow; never turn this into a broad freighter. The outline should feel predatory through shaped structural masses, without literal jaws or teeth.
Wings: broader at their inner root, distinct closed sliding sleeve and partly recessed hinge bearing, then sharply TAPERED forward-swept outer blades with a pronounced angular step in the leading edge and needle-like authored tip; a lean slashing profile, unlike D01's broad chisel tips. Both wing segments droop in flight, no upturned tips. Add deep red inset fields near the wing roots and one pale reclaimed outer wing surface per side. Major visual interest is the sculpted slanted shoulders, closed mechanical wing roots, cut-in waist and sharp forward blade silhouette, not added surface plating. Strong patchwork construction using large well-fitted donor sections; asymmetry allowed only in fixed service covers and colour, with symmetric mechanism and overall balanced mass. Charcoal lower housings, pale upper shoulder leading facets, muted oxblood side recesses. Single rear exhaust in short heavy angular housing.
Title exactly: DRAUGR / D02
